51476782.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human wild type adenosine A1 receptor expressed in Expi293F cells assessed as dissociation constant by surface plasmon resonance assay

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: The SPR A2A assay was validated using known activity probes such as the agonist adenosine, the antagonist ZM 241385, and three fragment-like molecules theophylline (mol wt = 180 Da), allopurinol (mol wt = 140 Da), and caffeine (mol wt = 195 Da). The binding sensorgrams obtained are shown in Figure 1A,B. Binding affinities and kinetic parameters are summarized in Table 1 and correspond well to the literature results. Although the response levels for fragments were low, it was possible to detect fragments as small as 140 Da with affinities ranging from 3.6 to 77 μM.
original_paragraph.Adenosine Receptor Selectivity Assay: To determine whether the fragment hits showed selectivity to the A2A receptor relative to the remaining adenosine receptor family, we developed SPR-based assays for adenosine receptors A1, A2B, and A3. To assess the conformational activity of the receptors, we screened classically selective (Table 1) ligands for each receptor and compared the results to literature data. Binding sensorgrams for SLV320, CV1808, LUF5834, and adenosine binding to A1, A2A, A2B, and A3, respectively, are shown in Figure 2C–F. Binding affinities are summarized in Table 1 and correspond well to literature data.
original_paragraph.Figure 1 caption: Figure 1. (A) Binding sensorgrams of control compounds adenosine (left) and ZM 241385 (right). Adenosine was injected from 7.8 nM to 1 μM, and ZM 241385 was injected in concentration series from 91.4 pM to 200 nM. Black lines represent binding sensorgrams, and red lines represent 1:1 kinetic fit. (B) Binding sensorgrams of fragment-like compounds theophylline (1), allopurinol (2), and caffeine (3) injected at a concentration series from 0.823 to 200 μM. Affinity was calculated using equilibrium 1:1 binding model.
original_paragraph.Figure 2 caption: Figure 2. (A) Responses of fragments binding to the A2A receptor (black squares), reference 1 (red empty circle) and reference 2 (blue empty triangle) read immediately prior to the end of injection. (B) Binding responses of positive control, theophylline (solid symbols), and negative control, sulpiride (empty symbols), binding to the A2A receptor (square) and reference proteins (circle, triangle). (C) Binding sensorgrams of SLV320 binding to the A1 receptor at a 3-fold concentration series ranging from 4.57 nM to 10 μM. (D) Binding sensorgrams of CV1808 binding to the A2A receptor at a 3-fold concentration series ranging from 4.57 nM to 10 μM. (E) Binding sensorgrams of LUF5834 binding to the A2B receptor at a 3-fold concentration series ranging from 4.57 nM to 10 μM. (F) Binding sensorgrams of adenosine binding to the A3 receptor at a 3-fold concentration series ranging from 0.0457 to 100 μM. Black lines represent binding sensorgrams for each concentration, and red lines are a 1:1 kinetic fit.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: The SPR A2A assay was validated using known activity probes such as the agonist adenosine, the antagonist ZM 241385, and three fragment-like molecules theophylline (mol wt = 180 Da), allopurinol (mol wt = 140 Da), and caffeine (mol wt = 195 Da). The binding sensorgrams obtained are shown in Figure 1A,B. Binding affinities and kinetic parameters are summarized in Table 1 and correspond well to the literature results. Although the response levels for fragments were low, it was possible to detect fragments as small as 140 Da with affinities ranging from 3.6 to 77 μM.
original_paragraph.Adenosine Receptor Selectivity Assay: To determine whether the fragment hits showed selectivity to the A2A receptor relative to the remaining adenosine receptor family, we developed SPR-based assays for adenosine receptors A1, A2B, and A3. To assess the conformational activity of the receptors, we screened classically selective (Table 1) ligands for each receptor and compared the results to literature data. Binding sensorgrams for SLV320, CV1808, LUF5834, and adenosine binding to A1, A2A, A2B, and A3, respectively, are shown in Figure 2C–F. Binding affinities are summarized in Table 1 and correspond well to literature data.
original_paragraph.Figure 1 caption: Figure 1. (A) Binding sensorgrams of control compounds adenosine (left) and ZM 241385 (right). Black lines represent binding sensorgrams, and red lines represent 1:1 kinetic fit. (B) Binding sensorgrams of fragment-like compounds theophylline (1), allopurinol (2), and caffeine (3) injected at a concentration series from 0.823 to 200 μM. original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) experiments were performed on a Biacore S200 (Cytiva) using CM5 sensor chips (Cytiva). Human wild-type adenosine receptors A1, A2A, A2B, and A3 were expressed in Expi293F cells and purified as described previously.17,18 The receptors were immobilized on the sensor chip via amine coupling. Binding assays were performed in HBS-EP+ buffer (10 mM HEPES, pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 3 mM EDTA, 0.005% P20) at 25 °C. Compounds were injected at concentrations ranging from 0.823 to 200 μM for fragment library screening and from 0.0457 to 100 μM for kinase library screening. The association phase lasted 60 s, followed by a 120 s dissociation phase. Reference surfaces were prepared by immobilizing the same amount of protein on a separate flow cell. Data were analyzed using Biacore Evaluation Software 3.0. Binding affinities were calculated using a 1:1 binding model. For selectivity profiling, fragments were screened against all four adenosine receptors. For the A2B receptor, binding was assessed as affinity off-rate by SPR assay. The dissociation phase was extended to 120 s to allow for accurate measurement of off-rates. The kinetic parameters were determined by fitting the sensorgrams to a 1:1 binding model using Biacore Evaluation Software 3.0.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - SPR assay: Purified wild-type A2AR was captured via the His tag on a Biacore Series S nickel-NTA sensor chip in running buffer (50 mM HEPES pH 7.0, 150 mM NaCl, 50 μM EDTA, 0.1% DDM, 0.1% CHAPS, 0.02% CHS, 3% DMSO), to obtain capture levels 5,000 – 6,000 RU. Analysis temperature was set to 10 °C and the sample compartment to 15 °C to maintain stability of the receptor on the surface. To increase the stability of the receptor, hA2AR was crosslinked to the surface by a 15 min injection of 1:1 ratio of 400 mM 1-ethyl-3-(3-dimethylaminopropyl) carbodiimide hydrochloride (EDC) and 100 mM N-hydroxy succinimide (NHS) prior to the capture of A2A onto activated Ni2+ surface. To confirm receptor activity, binding of an agonist (adenosine) and antagonist (ZM241385) were measured by injecting ligands over the surface at 30 μL/min for 60 s and allowing to dissociate for 180 s. Adenosine was injected from 7.8 nM – 1 μM and ZM 241385 was injected in concentration series from 91.4 pM – 200 nM. To confirm assay sensitivity, tool fragments theophylline, caffeine and allopurinol were injected in concentration series from 0.823 – 200 μM. Theophylline and sulpiride were injected at 100 μM concentrations at 60-minute intervals for 35 hours to test stability of captured vs. capture-coupled receptor.
original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Fragment hits co: Purified wild-type A1, A2A, A2B and A3 were captured via His-tag on an NTA sensor chip surface in running buffer (50 mM HEPES pH 7.0, 150 mM NaCl, 50 μM EDTA, 0.1% DDM, 0.1% CHAPS, 0.02% CHS (-CHS for A1 receptor), 3% DMSO), to obtain capture levels 4,000 – 6,000 RU for A2A, A2B and A3 and ~ 10,000 RU for A1 receptors. Activity of captured receptors was assessed using control compounds SLV320 (A1 receptor), CV1808 (A2A receptor), LUF5834 (A2B receptor) and adenosine (A3 receptor) at 3-fold concentration series ranging from 4.57 nM - 10 μM for A1, A2A and A2B and 0.0457 – 100 μM for A3 compounds. Selected A2A receptor fragment hits were screened in 3-fold concentration series with top concentrations ranging from 333 nM - 10 μM depending on compound affinity. Flow rate was set to 30 μL/min. Association and dissociation was measured for 60 s and 60 – 180 s, respectively. All experiments were run at 10 °C.

Affinity fit of fragments binding to the A2A receptor. C. Affinity fit of fragments binding to the A2B receptor. D. Affinity fit of fragments binding to the A3 receptor. E. Kinetic fit for fragment J binding to the A2A receptor. Black traces represent binding sensorgrams, orange traces represent 1:1 kinetic fit. Kinetic parameters were obtained at ka = 1.03 (± 0.02) x 104 M-1s-1, kd = 0.036 (± 0.05) s-1 and KD = 3.45 (± 0.02) μM.
original_paragraph.Figure S3 caption: Figure S3. NECA binding to the A2A receptor. NECA was injected in a 3-fold concentration series from 4.6 nM to 10 μM. Black lines represent sensorgrams and orange lines 1:1 kinetic fit.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: The SPR assay was performed on a Biacore S200 (Cytiva) using human wild-type A3 receptor expressed in Expi293F cells and immobilized on a CM5 sensor chip (Cytiva) as described previously.17,18 The receptor was immobilized at a level of 1000–1500 response units (RU) using amine coupling.
